newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Colombo auction tea prices rise on better demand.
newsitem.headline: Colombo auction tea prices rise on better demand.

text.p: Tea prices rose at the Colombo auction on improved demand and a global fall in the crop, brokers said on Wednesday.
"There was better demand. We've been having fairly small sales because of the (traditional new year) holidays and shorter weeks," said a broker at Eastern Brokers.
"Also worldwide, prices at most auctions have moved up because production has dropped, especially in Kenya," he added.
The anticipated gross auction average price for the 4.7 million kg on offer rose to 115 rupees ($1.94) per kg from 114.84 rupees last week, Forbes and Walker said.
Crop intakes are expected to improve as bright mornings with evening showers -- the ideal weather for tea -- have been reported from most planting districts, they said.
The crop fell in the first quarter because of very dry weather, they said.
The next auction is on May 6-7 where 4.8 million kg will be on offer. ($1=59.22 rupees) --Colombo newsroom (941) 434319
